title: Works, but wastes 1/4 of the juice. Quiet and easily cleaned. Lots of parts
text:
Works, but wastes 1/4 of the juice. Quiet and easily cleaned. Lots of parts. Let me just say up front, we aren't typically inclined to juice. I mean, we drink juice and we eat fruit, but we buy it ready made for many reasons. Not the least of which is convenience. This machine was my way of trying to do some stuff at home to save a bit of money and perhaps time when compared to the old hand juicers or buying it.

I was a little taken aback by the size of this machine - it's really big and next to our full size Kureig coffee machine it requires the same amount of counter space. That's a big footprint. Dragging it in and out of the pantry means handling several loose parts each time, but leaving it in place full time makes the kitchen look cluttered.

I have made several different juices with this and it handled everything easily. We have done orange and pineapple, mango and pineapple, papaya and grapefruit (gross), and just plain limes to mix with tequila later tonight. (Don't judge, who has time to squeeze a lime when there's drinking to be done?) You have to peel everything, remove the cores and the seeds and then you can put the fruit in the machine. Honestly, it's considerably less work to use an old hand juicer and less messy. Nonetheless, the juice tastes good - it does froth like crazy though. I'll give them credit, the motor is very quiet.

My issue here is the amount of wasted juice in the pulp catcher. Easily a quarter of the juice goes in the waste catcher rather your glass or pitcher. That irks me after all the work/time to clean, peel, cut and juice the fruit. Especially an entire pineapple! For our regular, daily consumption, this isn't worth the effort. I would rather just buy cut fruit and eat it on the go because it's faster, easier and I get all of it.
